correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs local quotient valuations as digit carries and counts exact maximal residues; CRT gives exact density. Analytically, small primes contribute o(k/log k), large primes reduce to log fractional parts of (k+1)/p. A logarithmic truncation estimate using Brun–Titchmarsh, uniform PNT with total variation, and an absolutely convergent integral yield the stated explicit C. Independent finite arithmetic checks cover every prime factor for k<300 and complete periods for k<=12; finite checks are supporting, not proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General multiplicative least-period and arithmetic-progression exact distribution results subsume the function and finite densities but do not supply a uniform k-parameter asymptotic. No claim of new periodicity or finite frequency is made.

originality.rationale: The genuinely new statement is the sharp growing-window logarithmic density rate, not the covered finite carry count. Full primary text of Huang–Yang addresses least periods, while full published value-frequency record gives fixed-k distributions but neither claims nor derives an asymptotic for k growing. The lcm-binomial equality record concerns a different event. Targeted semantic, alias and parameter searches found no direct covering theorem. An unindexed analytic derivation is the live originality risk.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent unindexed earlier analytic asymptotic may exist.
The primary 2009 Hong–Qian full PDF was not separately read; the published exact-value record was read completely.
The finite frequency formula is explicitly prior-covered and cannot itself support novelty.

value.rationale: The extremal value k! is the natural global envelope of a classical Farhi periodic quotient. Its frequency for growing window k is mathematically distinct from fixed-k tables and least periods. The sharp universal decay constant settles its first-order arithmetic rarity at the intrinsic prime scale k/log k. This uses substantive prime-distribution and singular-logarithm estimates rather than a routine finite local calculation.
